stories.headline: Africa Intelligence Brief for Friday, May 8, 2026 Today's Africa intelligence brief opens with Mali Foreign Minister Abdoulaye Diop ruling out any negotiation with jihadist groups as Bloomberg
stories.summary: Mali's Foreign Minister Abdoulaye Diop has ruled out negotiations with jihadist groups, citing concerns that dialogue could expand the conflict in the region. The decision comes as the country faces ongoing instability and violence from al-Qaeda-linked jihadists in its central and northern regions. The Malian government has maintained its stance against negotiating with terrorist groups, which it holds responsible for years of tragic events. Meanwhile, the country's institutions and security forces remain operational, despite attempts to overthrow the authorities. The announcement by Diop reaffirms the government's commitment to combating terrorism, as it continues to face challenges from militant groups, including the Azawad Liberation Front, which has been allied with jihadists in the past. The situation remains volatile, with recent discoveries of militant groups in areas such as the village of Gossi.

stories.headline: ABC says Trump’s FCC is threatening free speech in ‘The View’ probe ABC is accusing the Trump administration’s media regulator of threatening broadcasters’ First Amendment rights.
stories.summary: ABC has accused the Trump administration's Federal Communications Commission (FCC) of threatening free speech in its probe of "The View," a daytime talk show. In a legal letter to the FCC, the network claims the agency's actions could "upend decades of settled law and practice and chill critical protected speech." The issue at hand is the FCC's investigation into "The View," which has become a platform for discussion and debate on various topics. ABC argues that the FCC's actions threaten broadcasters' First Amendment rights, potentially stifling critical speech and setting a troubling precedent. The network's petition was filed on May 7, sparking concerns about the impact on free speech and the media industry. The FCC's investigation and ABC's response highlight the ongoing debate over the regulation of speech and the role of government in overseeing the media.

stories.headline: Ethiopia’s petroleum officials among 13 charged in alleged fuel diversion scheme Prosecutors allege that the defendants diverted gasoline and white diesel outside government oversight, exacerbating fuel shortages in the domestic market.
stories.summary: Ethiopian prosecutors have charged 13 individuals, including petroleum officials, in an alleged fuel diversion scheme. The defendants are accused of diverting gasoline and white diesel outside government oversight, exacerbating fuel shortages in the domestic market. The alleged scheme involved the disappearance of 68 fuel tankers in July 2025, with millions of liters of fuel funneled to the black market. The prosecution claims the actions had a direct, negative impact on citizens' daily lives, contributing to chronic fuel shortages and long queues at gas stations. Evidence includes the diversion of fuel to unlicensed entities and the manipulation of the market for profit. The case is part of a broader crackdown on corruption and economic sabotage, with authorities seizing contraband fuel and uncovering smuggling and hoarding networks across the country.

stories.headline: Army eyes affordable surveillance with Baltic balloon test U.S. soldiers will launch a micro high-altitude balloon from Sweden, with the mission concluding in Latvia following roughly 30 hours of flight.
stories.summary: US soldiers are launching a micro high-altitude balloon from Sweden as part of a test for affordable surveillance in the Baltic region. The mission is expected to conclude in Latvia after approximately 24 to 30 hours of flight. The high-altitude balloon platform is designed for persistent sensing and communications missions. The test is part of a training exercise with NATO partners in the region. The US Army is exploring the use of high-altitude balloons as a cost-effective alternative for surveillance, similar to the capabilities of the Northrop Grumman RQ-4 Global Hawk, a high-altitude UAV used by the Air Force. The balloon will fly at an altitude of around 70,000 feet, providing a platform for surveillance and communications over a wide area. The test aims to demonstrate the feasibility of using high-altitude balloons for persistent surveillance in the region.

stories.headline: 'Dirty Frag' Gives Root on Linux Distros Security researchers have discovered a new, critical flaw in the Linux kernel that attackers can exploit to gain root access. No patches are yet available to fi
stories.summary: A critical flaw in the Linux kernel, known as "Dirty Frag," has been discovered, allowing attackers to gain root access on most major Linux distributions. The vulnerability, identified as CVE-2026-43284, is a local privilege escalation issue that can be exploited with a single command. No patches are currently available to fix the issue. The vulnerability was publicly disclosed on May 8, 2026, after an embargo was broken, granting hackers immediate root access. Mitigations are now available, but a patch has not been released yet. The Dirty Frag vulnerability affects most Linux distros, making it a significant security concern. Security researchers have warned users to be cautious, as attackers can exploit this vulnerability to gain elevated privileges on affected systems. Users are advised to apply available mitigations until a patch is released.

stories.headline: Emergent Vision Unveils 4D Gaussian Splatting & High-Speed Cameras Learn more about a recent demo of a cutting-edge 36-camera array in action
stories.summary: Emergent Vision Technologies showcased a 36-camera array at NAB 2026, demonstrating cutting-edge 4D Gaussian splatting capabilities. The multi-server system utilizes GPUDirect processing for high-resolution volumetric capture, rendering out a 4D Gaussian splat in real-time. The company featured three demos, including live 4D Gaussian splatting in the 36-camera EROS array, and showcased their lineup of high-speed, high framerate GigE camera systems. This technology unifies spatio-temporal Gaussian primitives for real-time dynamic scene modeling and photorealistic rendering from multi-view video. Emergent's system can record timecode-aligned 3840 x 2160 resolution video at 30 frames per second, capturing complex human motions and interactions with high accuracy. The demo highlighted the potential of 4D Gaussian splatting for advanced applications in fields such as computer vision and virtual reality.

stories.headline: iQOO Neo12 key specs tipped, may offer an active cooling fan The handset could be powered by the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 SoC. iQOO is reportedly working on the new Neo12 for China, according to a recent leak....
stories.summary: The iQOO Neo12 is reportedly in testing, with key specs including the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 SoC and a potential 2K resolution display. The device may also feature an active cooling fan. Tipster Smart Pikachu shared the information on Weibo, indicating the phone is currently being tested. If released, the iQOO Neo12 would be a new addition to the iQOO lineup in China. The Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 SoC is a high-performance processor, suggesting the Neo12 could be positioned as a gaming or flagship device. Previous iQOO models, such as the iQOO 12 and iQOO Neo 11, have featured similar high-end specs, including large displays, high-capacity batteries, and ample storage and RAM options. The iQOO Neo12's exact release date and full specs have not been officially confirmed.

stories.headline: Path of Exile 2: Return of the Ancients Redefines The Endgame Experience on May 29 Press releases and assets from across the games industry - screenshots, videos, logos, packshots, artwork, PR contacts, release dates
stories.summary: Path of Exile 2: Return of the Ancients is set to launch on May 29, bringing the largest update to the game yet. This update completely revamps the endgame experience, introducing over 50 hours of new content. The update includes a new challenge system, powerful unique items, expanded crafting systems, and a reimagined Atlas Tree. The launch will be available on PC, Steam, PlayStation, Xbox, and the Epic Games Store. The update aims to provide a more cohesive and intentional experience, addressing player concerns about the game's complexity and endgame progression. With a significant amount of new content, players can expect a fresh and engaging experience, building towards the final classes, ascendancies, and acts expected by the end of the year. The update is highly anticipated, with many players expressing excitement and relief at the changes.

stories.headline: Bruno Fernandes pips Declan Rice to FWA Men’s Footballer of the Year
stories.summary: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has won the Football Writers' Association men's Footballer of the Year award for the 2025-26 season. He secured 45% of the votes from the FWA's membership of over 900 members. Fernandes narrowly beat Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice, who finished second by just 28 votes. Manchester City striker Erling Haaland came in third. This is the first time a Manchester United player has received the honor since Wayne Rooney in 2010, and the first time in nine years the award has gone to a player outside of the traditional top contenders. Fernandes, 31, received the award for his outstanding performance during the 2025-26 season.

stories.headline: Olympic water polo resignations cite lack of respect, belittling behaviour
stories.summary: Olympic water polo team members have resigned, citing a lack of respect and belittling behavior from the new federation president, Slobodan Soro. The team, current European and triple Olympic champions, stated that Soro's comments have attempted to discredit their past successes. Coach Stevanovic also resigned, citing Soro's use of unbecoming language towards the team. The resignations come amid controversy surrounding the sport, including a recent statement from the NOC*NSF regarding unforeseen attention to trauma from sexual offences and cross-border behavior. The water polo team's decision to speak out highlights the tension within the federation, with the team feeling disrespected and undervalued by the new leadership. The resignations have significant implications for the sport, given water polo's long history in the Olympics, dating back to 1900. Hungary and the US have been dominant forces in the men's and women's tournaments.

stories.headline: How and when can Arsenal or Man City win the Premier League?
stories.summary: The Premier League title race is nearing its conclusion, with Arsenal and Manchester City as the top contenders. The two teams have remaining fixtures that will determine the champion. Arsenal currently holds an edge, but Manchester City can still top the table. The title race is going down to the final day for only the 10th time in history. Pep Guardiola's Manchester City, who have won the Premier League five times under his leadership, are looking to claim the trophy again. Meanwhile, Arsenal is seeking to win the title. The outcome will be decided this weekend, with both teams having crucial matches that will ultimately determine the Premier League champion. The final day of the season will see one of these two teams emerge as the winner, ending the intense title race.

stories.headline: Brook back as Yorkshire dominate Warwickshire Harry Brook is 29 not out in his first game of the summer as Yorkshire reach stumps on 110-4 after bowling out Warwickshire for 147 et Edgbaston.
stories.summary: Yorkshire dominated Warwickshire on day one at Edgbaston, bowling out the home side for 147. England's Harry Brook made his return to county cricket, finishing unbeaten on 29. At stumps, Yorkshire reached 110-4, taking control of the match. The visitors' strong bowling performance set the tone for the day, restricting Warwickshire to a low total. Brook's unbeaten 29 in his first game of the summer provided a solid foundation for Yorkshire's innings. Both teams have similar records this season, with one win, one loss, and two draws from four matches. Warwickshire sits fourth in the Division One table with 55 points, while Yorkshire is seventh with 40 points. The match is part of the County Championship, with Yorkshire looking to build on their strong start.

stories.headline: AI-171 crash probe in final stage, civil aviation min says report likely in a month Investigation into Air India Flight AI 171 crash that killed 260 people in Ahmedabad last year is in its final stage, report is expected within a month, Union c
stories.summary: The investigation into the Air India Flight AI 171 crash that killed 260 people in Ahmedabad last year is in its final stage. According to Union Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu, the report is expected to be completed within a month. The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) is conducting the probe with full resources from the ministry. A preliminary report had indicated that fuel supply to both engines was cut off within a second after take-off, causing cockpit confusion. The final report will undergo international scrutiny due to the presence of foreign nationals on the flight. The AAIB is working to complete the investigation, and the report is likely to be released soon, providing closure to the families of the victims and shedding light on the cause of the tragic accident.

stories.headline: A year after Operation Sindoor, China admits helping Pakistan's air force during confrontation with India: Report For the first time, China has confirmed that it assisted Pakistan by providing on-site technical support during its war with India last year.
stories.summary: China has publicly acknowledged providing on-ground technical assistance to Pakistan during last year's conflict with India, following Operation Sindoor. This is the first time China has confirmed its involvement in the confrontation. The assistance was given to Pakistan's air force, with China providing on-site technical support. The admission comes a year after the operation, marking a significant development in the region's geopolitical dynamics. The confirmation highlights the close ties between China and Pakistan, particularly in the defense sector. China's support to Pakistan during the conflict underscores the complexities of the India-Pakistan-China triangle, with potential implications for regional stability and security. The acknowledgement is a notable shift in China's stance, as it had not previously publicly disclosed its role in the conflict.

stories.headline: TTV Dhinakaran of AMMK meets Governor, seeks invite for AIADMK govt TTV Dhinakaran met the Governor backing AIADMK’s claim, alleging his lone MLA is missing amid suspected horse-trading, adding fresh tension as rival bids intens
stories.summary: TTV Dhinakaran, General Secretary of Amma Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam (AMMK), met the Governor of Tamil Nadu to extend support to All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK)'s Edappadi Karuppa Palaniswami to form the state government. Dhinakaran alleged that his lone MLA, S Kamaraj, is missing amid suspected horse-trading by rival parties. He handed over a letter to the Governor stating that E. Palaniswami enjoys the support of his party. This development adds fresh tension to the government formation race in Tamil Nadu, where rival bids are intensifying. Dhinakaran's move is seen as a blow to actor-turned-politician Vijay Thalapathy, who had also staked a claim to form the government. The Governor's next move is awaited as the political landscape in Tamil Nadu continues to unfold.

stories.headline: Suvendu Adhikari's swearing in: Date, time, and guest list as West Bengal gets its first BJP CM India News: NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Friday chose Suvendu Adhikari to be the next chief minister of West Bengal after saffron party's resoundi
stories.summary: Suvendu Adhikari is being sworn in as the Chief Minister of West Bengal, the first BJP leader to hold the top post in the state. The swearing-in ceremony took place on May 9 at Brigade Parade. Adhikari was chosen by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) after their resounding victory in the state, securing 207 seats. He met with West Bengal Governor R N Ravi and staked claim to form the government. Adhikari's appointment marks a significant shift in the state's politics, ending 15 years of Mamata Banerjee's rule. The ceremony is a grand affair, with a notable guest list. Adhikari has vowed to restore Bengali pride and focus on work, stating "Less Talk, More Work" in his first address after being named the Chief Minister of West Bengal.

stories.headline: AI investments begin paying off for big tech companies Strong Mag 7 earnings and AI gains continue supporting markets despite concerns over oil prices, geopolitics and consumer confidence.
stories.summary: The Magnificent Seven tech companies have reported stronger-than-expected quarterly earnings, driven by investments in artificial intelligence (AI). Alphabet's shares gained 7% after its earnings report, with Google Search revenue growing 19% and defying expectations that AI would erode its core advertising business. The AI equipment segment saw a significant increase of 3.7%. The strong earnings reports have provided support for broader equity markets, despite concerns over oil prices, geopolitics, and consumer confidence. The results indicate that the billions invested in AI are paying off for big tech companies, with AI infrastructure spending contributing to the growth. However, concerns still linger in the stock market, and the adoption of AI agents in other industries, such as banking, remains limited due to trust issues. The AI boom is showing positive results, but its impact is still largely confined to the big tech sector.

stories.headline: Gold heads for weekly gain as markets watch US-Iran peace signals
stories.summary: Gold is heading for a weekly gain as markets respond to potential US-Iran peace signals. The precious metal rose on Friday, driven by easing fears of inflation and higher interest rates. Investors remain optimistic about a possible US-Iran peace deal, which has helped alleviate concerns about inflation and interest rates. Silver, platinum, and palladium also climbed this week. Analysts note that price moves may be uneven due to geopolitics and interest rate outlook. The weekly gain comes as investors weigh hopes for a peace agreement against ongoing uncertainties. Key factors to watch include Iran's confirmation of reviewing deal terms, oil prices holding below $105, and the US labor market showing signs of softening, as indicated by the upcoming nonfarm payrolls report. Gold's price movement is being closely monitored amid these developments.

stories.headline: Will Trump threaten Spain's sovereignty over Ceuta and Melilla?
stories.summary: A US congressional report has described Ceuta and Melilla as being located in Moroccan territory and "under Spanish administration", sparking concerns in Madrid about potential interference in Spain's sovereignty. The report, issued by a congressman affiliated with Donald Trump, has been interpreted in Morocco as a sign of US backing for Rabat's claims over the Spanish enclaves. Ceuta and Melilla have been part of Spanish territory for centuries and are fully integrated into the country's constitutional order. The description by the US House of Representatives committee has raised concerns in Spain, with Madrid considering any external questioning of its sovereignty as unacceptable interference. The incident has ignited a diplomatic row, with Morocco seeing it as a boost to its claims and Spain seeking to protect its territorial integrity.

stories.headline: Precious metals moved higher this week as markets tracked US-Iran peace signals
stories.summary: Precious metals prices increased as markets responded to potential US-Iran peace deal developments. Gold rose 0.6% to $1,720 per ounce is not mentioned, instead it says Gold rose 0.6% to $4,720 per ounce, while silver climbed 1.6% to $78.6. The gains came as US President Donald Trump indicated a possible peace deal with Iran may be near, following a ceasefire announcement. Trump stated Iran's uranium will be "perfectly taken care of" in an interview. The US dollar also strengthened, with the USD/JPY bouncing back after suspected intervention. US 10-year yields increased 2.4 basis points to 4.40%. The potential peace deal has led to a decrease in oil prices, supporting benchmark stock market indices to open higher, driven by stock-specific reactions to corporate earnings.

stories.headline: Sensex sinks 600 points: Why is the stock market falling today?
stories.summary: The Indian stock market experienced a significant decline, with the Sensex sinking nearly 600 points and the Nifty slipping below 17,200. Weak global cues, rising crude oil prices, and foreign investor selling contributed to the downturn. The Sensex recovered almost 850 points from its low of 23,083.18, trading around 150 points higher at 23,300. The market crash resulted in a loss of ₹7 lakh crore, exacerbated by a weak rupee and heavy foreign selling. Renewed US-Iran tension and recession fears also weighed on the market. The Nifty fell below the 17,200 mark, with banking stocks adding to the pressure. The decline is part of a global downturn triggered by tariff announcements and recession fears, leading to a sharp sell-off in Indian stock markets.

stories.headline: Market Wrap: Sensex drops 516 points, Nifty closes below 24,200 amid fresh Iran-US escalations, smallcaps outperform
stories.summary: The Sensex dropped 516 points to close at 77,328, while the Nifty 50 fell 150 points to 24,176. The decline was attributed to fresh Iran-US escalations, leading to profit booking in the market. Despite the overall downturn, the smallcap index defied the trend and closed in the green, outperforming the benchmarks. IT stocks gained, and crude oil prices remained above $100. The Bank Nifty traded below its 50 and 20-day simple moving averages, a negative indicator. The 50-day SMA at 56,000 is expected to be a key reference point for short-term traders. The market's decline was largely driven by geopolitical jitters, with the Sensex and Nifty falling amid escalating tensions between Iran and the US. Smallcap stocks, however, extended their rally, providing a contrasting trend in the market.

stories.headline: Stock market today: Sensex Cracks Over 500 Points, Nifty Slips Below 24,200 As Fresh Iran-US Tensions Rattle Dalal Street
stories.summary: The Indian stock market experienced a significant decline due to rising tensions between the US and Iran. The Sensex fell 516 points to 74,207.24, a 3.26% drop, while the Nifty decreased 146 points to 23,002.15. This represents the worst market crash since the Iran-US conflict began last month. The benchmark indices plummeted sharply during intraday trading, with the Sensex crashing over 2,300 points at one point. The Nifty also slipped below 23,000. The decline is attributed to the escalating tensions in West Asia, which has led to a risk-off mood across sectors. The oil price shock from the conflict has also rattled global markets, contributing to the sharp fall in the Indian stock market. The Sensex and Nifty had opened flat on Friday, with the Sensex around 79,900 and the Nifty near 24,200, before experiencing the significant decline.

stories.headline: Stock markets today: Sensex, Nifty50 slump in early trade Indian equity markets experienced a significant decline in early trade, with the BSE Sensex and NSE Nifty dropping, as escalating geopolitical tensions in West
stories.summary: Indian equity markets declined in early trade, with the BSE Sensex and NSE Nifty dropping due to escalating geopolitical tensions. The BSE Sensex fell 160.24 points to 77,798.28, while the NSE Nifty dipped 30.25 points to 24,300.70. Yesterday, the Sensex closed 516 points lower at 77,328.19, and the Nifty 50 settled at 23,176.15, down 151 points. The decline is attributed to renewed US-Iran tensions and profit booking. Despite initial gains on Wednesday due to lower crude oil prices and positive Asian market trends, the indices turned negative in the second half of trade. IT stocks gained, while crude oil remained above $100, contributing to the market volatility. The benchmark indices are trading between highs and lows, reflecting the uncertain market sentiment.

stories.headline: Apple and Intel reportedly reach preliminary chip Intel Foundry may build Apple chips under reported agreement
stories.summary: Apple and Intel have reached a preliminary agreement for Intel to manufacture some of the chips used in Apple devices. The deal comes after over a year of discussions and is seen as a significant boost to Intel's contract manufacturing business. According to reports, the partnership was encouraged by the Trump administration, which converted federal grants into equity to support the deal. This move aims to reduce reliance on Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) and marks a major shift in US chip manufacturing strategy. As a result of the agreement, Intel's shares surged. The partnership will see Intel's foundry, Intel Foundry, produce processors for Apple devices, although details of the specific chips and production timeline have not been disclosed. The deal is expected to have significant implications for the US tech industry.

stories.headline: Michael Burry says the market today feels like 'the last months of the 1999-2000 bubble'
stories.summary: Michael Burry, a renowned investor and hedge fund manager, has warned that the current US stock market resembles the final stages of the 1999-2000 dot-com bubble. He drew parallels between the market's fixation on artificial intelligence and the excessive speculation of the late 1990s. Burry, who correctly predicted the 2008 housing crisis, suggested that a significant correction could be imminent. He stated that the current market feels like "the last months of the 1999-2000 bubble," citing the rapid rise of the stock market, which is outpacing even the growth seen in 1999. Burry's comments come as the market continues to rise, with some sectors, such as chip stocks, experiencing parabolic growth, prompting concerns of a potential bubble. His warning has sparked attention, given his track record of predicting major market events.

stories.headline: NTT (NTTYY) Q2 FY2025 earnings recap: record revenue, higher profit, DOCOMO competition update, IOWN progress, data center REIT gains & guidance—read now.
stories.summary: NTT reported record revenue of ¥6.59 trillion in Q2 FY2025, a ¥226.1 billion increase year-over-year. Operating profit, however, declined by ¥30.7 billion to ¥120.3 billion due to erosion in fixed-line services and costs associated with reinforcing DOCOMO's customer base. The company also provided updates on its IOWN initiative and data center REIT gains. Additionally, NTT offered guidance for future performance. In the previous fiscal year, Q2 FY2024, the company's operating profit had declined, but the current fiscal year's record revenue indicates a positive trend. The earnings report highlights the company's efforts to navigate competition, particularly from DOCOMO, while investing in new technologies and expanding its data center business. Overall, NTT's Q2 FY2025 earnings demonstrate a mix of revenue growth and profit challenges.

stories.headline: Aehr Test Systems stock is up some 327% year to date.
stories.summary: Aehr Test Systems' stock has surged 327% year to date, outperforming major semiconductor companies like Nvidia, AMD, and Broadcom. The company manufactures machines and equipment used to test semiconductors, a crucial component in the production of electronic devices. As a result, Aehr Test Systems has seen significant growth in its stock value. The company's success can be attributed to the increasing demand for semiconductor testing equipment, driven by the growing need for reliable and efficient electronic devices. With its stock up 327% year to date, investors are now wondering if Aehr Test Systems is still a viable buy, considering its impressive performance so far this year. The company's role in the semiconductor industry has positioned it for potential continued growth.
